Correctly stated: this is the pointwise inequality ε(u) ≤ π(u) on the algebraic binary tensor product, with the standard constructions of the two seminorms.

I read the site's rendered signature and docstring at commit `715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927` and the source, including both definitions. [The statement](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/InjectiveSeminorm.lean#L132) compares seminorms on the same `E ⊗[𝕜] F`, for seminormed spaces over a nontrivially normed field. [The projective seminorm](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L63) takes the infimum of the sums of products of norms over finite tensor decompositions; this set is nonempty and bounded below. [The injective seminorm](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/InjectiveSeminorm.lean#L72) is the norm of the canonical operator from the continuous dual of E to F, taking a pure tensor to `f ↦ f(x) • y`.

This matches [BanachSpaceTheory B4](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/BanachSpaceTheory/README.md#L190) and Ryan, Introduction to Tensor Products of Banach Spaces, §§2.1 and 3.1, equations (2.2) and (3.1)–(3.2) ([text consulted](https://djvu.online/file/ATNjYmfESxgzE)). For every finite decomposition, the dual operator norm is at most the sum of products of norms, so taking the infimum gives the stated direction. The general-field statement is an inequality of seminorms; it does not claim definiteness or a Hahn–Banach dual formula over arbitrary fields.

Checked axes: object, convention, edge-cases, junk, vacuous, choice, generality, naming. In particular, zero tensors and zero/seminorm-degenerate factors are allowed; no completeness is required for this algebraic statement. The infimum is not over an empty family. No hypothesis assumes the inequality. The definitions do not depend on a selected tensor decomposition. Over ℝ/ℂ, the [unit-ball characterization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/InjectiveSeminorm.lean#L148) confirms the classical scalar-dual interpretation.

These establish cross-norm values and definiteness over ℝ/ℂ with the stated normed-space hypotheses.

Correctly stated: smooth homotopic maps induce equal pullback maps in every nonnegative de Rham degree, including when the source has boundary or corners. This is the precise result requested by [DifferentialGeometry §6.3](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/DifferentialGeometry/README.md#L796), using the cylinder homotopy of §5.4.

At `715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927` I read the site's signature/docstring, [the theorem and its hypotheses](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/DeRham/HomotopyInvariance.lean#L96), the slice-inclusion argument, and the definitions of the cohomology and induced map. [deRhamCohomology](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/DeRham/Basic.lean#L120) is homology of the actual complex of smooth real-valued forms. [map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/DeRham/Map.lean#L123) descends the usual pullback on closed forms. Thus the variance is H^k(M′) → H^k(M), not the reverse, and the conclusion is equality of these linear maps.

Checked object, convention, edge-cases, junk, vacuous, choice, generality and naming. The homotopy lives on M×Icc(0,1) with the product corner model; both endpoint equations are explicit. No boundaryless, orientation, compactness or finite-dimensionality hypothesis was silently inserted. The source is smooth and the target has the C² structure needed by this cohomology construction; f,g,F are smooth. k=0 is included: the source handles it through closed functions constant along each interval, while positive degrees use the cochain-homotopy identity. The equality is not assumed or hidden in a structure field. The quotient construction does not choose a cohomology representative in the assertion.

Correctly stated: the definition is the zeta distribution on positive integers, with the invalid-parameter convention explicitly required by [StandardDistributions §9.6](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/StandardDistributions/README.md#L1379).

I inspected the rendered declaration and [source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Zipf/Basic.lean#L49) at `715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927`, including `zipfWeightReal`, `zipfWeight`, and the definition's value. For s > 1 the measure is the sum of Dirac masses with weight k^(-s)/Re(ζ(s)); at k=0 the negative-power convention gives zero, and for s≤1 the entire measure is explicitly zero. The normalization is over positive integers, not over indices starting with weight one at zero. The positive-real zeta value cannot vanish on this domain. The result agrees with the [documented Zipf mass formula](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.zipf.html).

Checked object, convention, edge-cases, junk, vacuous, choice, generality and naming: the real exponent is unrestricted in the function type but probability is asserted only for s>1; zero-measure totalization is documented; the definition is a concrete weighted measure, with no assumed normalization and no arbitrary choice. The positive support is substantiated by [zipfMeasure_singleton_ne_zero_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Zipf/Basic.lean#L154).

Checks relevant to this infinite law: [isProbabilityMeasure_zipfMeasure](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Zipf/Basic.lean#L128), [zipfMeasure_singleton_zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Zipf/Basic.lean#L148), and [zipfMeasure_of_le_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Zipf/Basic.lean#L83) are present, relate directly to the definition, and have no sorry. I also inspected [integrable_pow_map_cast_zipfMeasure_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Zipf/Moments.lean#L86) and [integral_pow_map_cast_zipfMeasure](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Zipf/Moments.lean#L93): the natural moment threshold is m<s−1 and the value is the required zeta ratio.

Correctly stated: this is the inverse Gaussian measure with mean parameter μ and shape parameter λ, using the density required by [StandardDistributions §10.8](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/StandardDistributions/README.md#L1687).

I read the rendered signature/docstring and the [definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/InverseGaussian/Basic.lean#L370), and expanded its [density definitions](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/InverseGaussian/Basic.lean#L79) at `715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927`. The real density is √(λ/(2πx³)) exp(−λ(x−μ)²/(2μ²x)) when μ, λ and x are positive, and zero otherwise; `ENNReal.ofReal` then supplies the density for `volume.withDensity`. The exponent has the minus sign, μ² denominator and x denominator required by the standard convention. This is also the parameterization in [NIST's inverse Gaussian density reference](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman2/ch8/igpdf.pdf).

Checked object, convention, edge-cases, junk, vacuous, choice, generality and naming. In particular μ=0 and λ=0 yield zero measures, not Dirac laws; this follows the Layer 10 default [invalid-parameter convention](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/StandardDistributions/README.md#L1487). The open density carrier (0,∞) is compatible with topological support [0,∞); the endpoint does not acquire an atom. Neither normalization nor a claimed probability structure is assumed in the definition. There is no arbitrary selected representation.

Direct source checks: [isProbabilityMeasure_inverseGaussianMeasure_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/InverseGaussian/Basic.lean#L394) gives exactly μ>0 and λ>0; [inverseGaussianMeasure_of_not_pos](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/InverseGaussian/Basic.lean#L381) gives the invalid branch; [inverseGaussianMeasure_Iic_zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/InverseGaussian/Basic.lean#L412) gives the lower support bound. Each is present, directly concerns this definition, and has no sorry. The normalization proof links [integral_inverseGaussianPDFReal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/InverseGaussian/Basic.lean#L354) through the nonnegative-density integral to the probability theorem.

These are for other families and were not treated as tests of the inverse Gaussian definition.

Correctly stated: the definition has the standard exact-phase Siegel product, with no lost root of unity. It matches [ImaginaryQuadraticClassNumber H3.2](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/ImaginaryQuadraticClassNumber/README.md#L91) and equation (1.1) in [Koo–Shin, Generation of class fields by Siegel–Ramachandra invariants](https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.2253) ([text inspected](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=ab41f99be4505d8e63e0ccd11e5f00f72005c846&repid=rep1&type=pdf)).

I read the site's signature/docstring and [definition value](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/SiegelFunction.lean#L63) at `715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927`. The leading minus sign, exp(πi B₂(r₁)τ), exp(πi r₂(r₁−1)), isolated (1−w), and paired factors (1−q^(n+1)w)(1−q^(n+1)w⁻¹) all match. The natural-number index n+1 correctly starts the infinite product at one. `bernoulliFun 2` is the polynomial x²−x+1/6, as confirmed in the pinned Mathlib ZetaValues source; it is not a periodically reduced Bernoulli function. exp(−z) supplies the inverse of w without choosing a logarithm.

Checked object, convention, edge-cases, junk, vacuous, choice, generality and naming. The real pair r generalizes the source's rational pair while retaining the same analytic formula. The definition itself allows integer pairs; only nonvanishing requires r∉ℤ². The domain is all ℂ with a documented unspecified value outside the upper half-plane; the holomorphy and nonvanishing theorems restrict to Im τ>0. No modularity at arbitrary real r is asserted by the definition. Canonical exponentials avoid any branch-dependent complex power.

In particular the infinite product is justified on the intended domain, rather than accepted from its totalized `tprod` value alone.

Correctly stated as the unnormalized, ambient Lusternik–Schnirelmann category required by [AlgebraicTopology, categorical covers](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology/README.md#L1080). I read the site's rendered signature/docstring, the [infimum definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/LusternikSchnirelmann.lean#L214), and the underlying [cover structure](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/LusternikSchnirelmann.lean#L70). A cover consists of actual open subsets of X whose inclusions in X are nullhomotopic, and its union contains A. This is the intended ambient notion; intrinsic contractibility of each open is not imposed.

Axes checked: object, convention, edge-cases, junk, vacuous, choice, generality and naming. The infimum lies in ℕ∞, so no finite cover yields ∞ rather than a totalized natural-number default. Fin 0 allows the empty cover. The convention gives the empty set count0, a contractible nonempty space count1, and a discrete subset its extended cardinality; it correctly distinguishes disconnected spaces. There is no selected minimizing cover in the definition.

Correctly stated: [StandardDistributions §11.2](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/StandardDistributions/README.md#L2044) specifies the Gaussian law with entry covariance UᵢₖVⱼₗ and an explicit Dirac fallback for invalid row or column covariance. The [definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/MatrixNormal/Basic.lean#L64) does exactly this. I inspected the rendered signature/docstring and definition value in source, together with [matrixVecMeasurableEquiv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Matrix/MeasurableSpace.lean#L46). Column stacking indexes by (column,row), so V⊗U produces VⱼₗUᵢₖ, the required covariance; the inverse reads that same pair order.

Axes checked: object, convention, edge-cases, junk, vacuous, choice, generality and naming. Both covariance matrices are checked separately for positive semidefiniteness: checking only their tensor product would wrongly admit two negative definite parameters. Singular and zero covariance are allowed. The construction uses a measurable equivalence and the Gaussian law, with no arbitrary choice of density or inverse matrix.

Correctly stated: [StandardDistributions §10.14](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/StandardDistributions/README.md#L1828) defines the asymmetric Laplace law as m+E_r−E_l for independent exponentials, with l the left rate and r the right rate. The [definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/AsymmetricLaplace/Basic.lean#L293) is the pushforward of expMeasure r × expMeasure l by (x,y)↦m+x−y, with an explicit positivity guard. Product measure supplies the required independence. I read the rendered signature/docstring and the source definition and density.

Axes checked: object, convention, edge-cases, junk, vacuous, choice, generality and naming. The rates have not been interchanged: integrating out y gives lr/(l+r) exp(−r(x−m)) for x>m, while the left branch is lr/(l+r) exp(l(x−m)). This agrees with [the implemented density](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/AsymmetricLaplace/Basic.lean#L92) and the roadmap. Both branches have the same value at m. Invalid rates yield zero, explicitly documented as not a probability law; this follows the roadmap's totalization rules at lines113–117. The construction contains no choice of exponential random variables on an unspecified probability space.

Checks: §10.14 contains no tagged Check. Its equal-rate specialization passes as [asymmetricLaplaceMeasure_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/AsymmetricLaplace/Basic.lean#L605), with no sorry, giving Laplace scale r⁻¹. The invalid left/right branches also pass at [lines307](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/AsymmetricLaplace/Basic.lean#L307) and [313](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/AsymmetricLaplace/Basic.lean#L313). Layer10 Checks at line2011 are about other families, not this definition.

Not checked: local Lean compilation or the original Kotz–Kozubowski–Podgórski chapter. [SciPy's asymmetric-Laplace convention](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/tutorial/stats/continuous_laplace_asymmetric.html) was inspected as an independent density parameterization; the two-rate convention here is fixed by the roadmap.
Equal rates specialize to Laplace with reciprocal-rate scale.
Nonpositive left rate gives the documented zero measure.
